songs.name: Beat It On Down The Line

ai_show_review.summary: Epic 47‑min Lovelight jam, fiery Smokestack Lightning with Elvin Bishop
ai_show_review.blurb: The set is anchored by a marathon 47‑minute Turn On Your Lovelight that showcases Jerry’s soaring leads and a tight rhythm section. Guest spots from Elvin Bishop on Smokestack Lightning and a surprise guitar cameo on Beat It On Down The Line keep the momentum high. Overall performance is energetic despite Phil’s slightly loosened bass.
ai_show_review.review: June 6, 1969 at Fillmore West finds the Dead in top‑form for a one‑disc set that pivots around an astonishing 47‑minute Turn On Your Lovelight. Jerry Garcia, who was late to the early numbers, re‑enters for the Lovelight and his guitar tone literally saves the night, weaving lyrical solos through the extended jam while the dual drummers lock in a propulsive groove. Elvin Bishop’s gritty blues licks on Smokestack Lightning add an extra spark, and a guest guitarist drops in on Beat It On Down The Line to give that track a punchy lift. Phil Lesh admits he was “zonked” from spiked apple juice, resulting in bass lines that are looser than usual, but the overall energy remains high and the band rides the momentum with confidence.

best_recording.reason: Soundboard source with clear mix; captures the epic Lovelight jam and guest spots without major drop‑outs.
